body.statement:
If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^{m+k}\) is semialgebraic, then its coordinate projection
\[
\{y\in\mathbb R^k:\exists x\in\mathbb R^m,\ (x,y)\in S\}
\]
is semialgebraic.

source.verbatim_statement: There exists a quantifier-free formula, Ψ(Y), such that for any y ∈ R^ℓ, Φ(y) is true if and only if Ψ(y) is true.

upstream.citation: A. Tarski, A decision method for elementary algebra and geometry

attestation.note: Transcribed from the official arXiv:1409.1534v1 PDF, Section 2.1, Theorem 2.1, p. 5; applying it to an existential formula yields the coordinate-projection instance.
